subject: Service unavailable window — request for SLA appeal and formal postmortem
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan@uptondigital.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: [Upton] Service interruption 2026-07-13 23:30-01:10 UTC — SLA credit request

Hi Olga / Marcus,

We observed a service outage affecting our production environment last night. Between 2026-07-13 23:30 UTC and 2026-07-14 01:10 UTC our requests to the /generate endpoint returned 502/504s and timeouts. The issue impacted customer-facing features and triggered automated failover for some sessions.

We're collecting the request ids and screenshots now (attached). Please confirm:
- Can Redwood validate that the observed window constitutes unavailability under our SLA?
- If so, what is the process and timeline for calculating any eligible service credit?
- We also need a postmortem with root cause, scope (routes/endpoints affected), and mitigation plan.

I attached a small ZIP with frontend error screenshots and a CSV with request IDs we captured. We are in the middle of an invoice dispute and need a formal statement for our finance team.

Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Thanks,
Megan Liu
Director of Engineering | Upton Digital
support@uptondigital.com

Attachments: upton-error-screenshots.zip, upton-request-ids.csv
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan@uptondigital.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Upton] Service interruption 2026-07-13 23:30-01:10 UTC — SLA credit request

Hi Megan,

Thanks — we've received the attachments and I've started the escalation to our SRE team. Quick acknowledgements and immediate next steps: 

1) Receipt confirmed. We'll validate the request IDs against our logs and confirm the exact availability window.
2) I've looped in Marcus from SRE to start a preliminary timeline — Marcus, can you confirm whether we see any cluster events or autoscaler activity in that window?
3) We'll assemble an initial incident header (window, affected routes, estimated error-rate) within 6 business hours and follow with a formal postmortem within 3 business days.

For our calculation we may need:
- Any client-side retry logic that could have masked duration (you included request IDs which is great)
- Whether you were pinned to a specific model version / instance pool (helps determine fallback behavior)

I'll keep you updated and will include the formal credit eligibility explanation once we've validated the exact downtime and SLO definitions.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai

> On Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 08:22 AM Megan Liu <megan@uptondigital.com> wrote:
> > We observed a service outage affecting our production environment last night.
> > Between 2026-07-13 23:30 UTC and 2026-07-14 01:10 UTC our requests to the /generate endpoint returned 502/504s and timeouts.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan@uptondigital.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Upton] Service interruption — preliminary incident assessment

Hi Megan, Olga,

SRE preliminary findings (high level):

- Observed behavior: between 2026-07-13 23:28 UTC and 2026-07-14 01:08 UTC we see a sustained spike in 502/504 errors and request timeouts for the customer-facing cluster serving Upton's workloads. The error-rate peaked ~23:50 UTC.
- Root cause (initial): autoscaler instability during a burst of traffic caused node churn; this in turn caused multiple in-flight KV-cache invalidations and cold-starts for a subset of pinned model instances. The combination increased tail latency and generated transient 5xx responses.
- Confirmed downtime window: 2026-07-13T23:28:00Z — 2026-07-14T01:08:00Z (1h40m). We are still cross-checking with the request ids you provided.

SLA impact and next steps:
- Based on the 1h40m unavailability window for your routed endpoints, this appears to meet the definition of unavailability under Section 2.3 of our SLA for production clusters. We will complete the formal credit eligibility calculation once log reconciliation is complete.
- I've attached a short timeline PDF (prelim-incident-timeline.pdf) with cluster events and autoscaler logs for the window.
- We will produce a full postmortem within 72 hours that includes root cause, blast radius, exact affected routes, and remediation plans (autoscaler tuning + improved graceful drain).

Please let us know if you need a CSV export of per-route request counts and latencies for your finance/invoice dispute — we can provide that as a Drive link within 24 hours.

Apologies for the impact — we'll treat this with priority.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai

Attachments: prelim-incident-timeline.pdf
From: Megan Liu <megan@uptondigital.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Upton] Service interruption — next steps and credit calculation request

Thanks for the quick assessment Marcus / Olga.

This confirms what our engineers saw. Two action items from our side:
1) Please provide the formal credit calculation and the SLA clause you're applying (we need the math and the date ranges for our records).
2) Please schedule the postmortem meeting — we'd like the primary SRE and a product owner on the call. Ideal window: Thu 2026-07-16 between 09:00-11:00 PT.

Also, please share the per-route export and any request-level logs you used for reconciliation; we'll attach those to our internal dispute.

If it helps, our finance contact is:
Eliot Park <eliot.park@uptondigital.com> — loop him into the credit calculation email.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Megan
